user.title: Add a Google TV
user.description: With the Raineworks TV app on the TV, enter the IP address its Home screen shows and submit: the TV asks to connect, and Allow there adds it. Without the app, turn on Settings → System → Developer options → USB debugging on the TV (and Network or Wireless debugging where it's a separate switch); when you submit, the TV shows "Allow USB debugging?": tick Always allow and choose Allow. This waits up to a minute for it.

data_description.host: The TV's IP address or host name.
data_description.port: The TV's ADB port, 5555 unless you changed it.
data_description.name: Optional. The TV's maker and model when empty.
data_description.install_tv_app: Raineworks TV on the TV: Home Assistant's notifications there. Installed over ADB once the TV is added.

pick.title: Add a TV
pick.description: These TVs have the Raineworks TV app and aren't in Home Assistant yet. Pick one and submit: the TV asks to connect, and **Allow** there adds it.

reauth_confirm.title: Reconnect {name}
reauth_confirm.description: {name} no longer trusts Home Assistant (debugging was turned off and on, or the TV was reset). Make sure USB debugging is on, submit, then tick Always allow and choose Allow on the TV.

enable_debugging.title: Turn on network debugging on {name}
enable_debugging.description:
Home Assistant reaches {name} ({host}) over network debugging, which is off. On the TV:

1. Settings → System → About: select **Android TV OS build** seven times ("You are now a developer").
2. Settings → System → Developer options: turn on **USB debugging**, and **Network debugging** (or Wireless debugging) where it's a separate switch.

Then submit. The TV app's screen shows these steps too.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Add {name}
zeroconf_confirm.description: {name} ({host}) has network debugging on. Submit, then on the TV tick Always allow and choose Allow when it asks "Allow USB debugging?". This waits up to a minute for it.

data_description.install_tv_app: Raineworks TV on the TV: Home Assistant's notifications there. Installed over ADB once the TV is added.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure {name}
reconfigure.description: Change {name}'s address or ADB port. If the TV asks "Allow USB debugging?", tick Always allow and choose Allow.

data_description.host: The TV's IP address or host name.
data_description.port: The TV's ADB port, 5555 unless you changed it.

app_confirm.title: Add {name}
app_confirm.description:
{name} ({host}) has the TV app. When you submit, the TV asks "Allow Home Assistant to connect?": choose **Allow** with the remote. This waits up to two minutes.

No developer options needed. For the remote's keys, turning the TV off and knowing its HDMI input, you can connect it over ADB later (Reconfigure).

reauth_app.title: Reconnect {name}
reauth_app.description: The TV app on {name} no longer knows Home Assistant (it was reinstalled, or its data cleared). Submit, then choose **Allow** on the TV.

connect_adb.title: Connect {name} over ADB
connect_adb.description:
ADB adds the remote's keys (D-pad, OK, Back, Home), turning the TV off and on, and which HDMI input is on screen; it also allows the TV app's permissions where the TV hides them.

1. On the TV: Settings → System → About, select **Android TV OS build** seven times.
2. Settings → System → Developer options: turn on **USB debugging**, and **Network debugging** where it's separate.
3. Submit, then on the TV tick **Always allow** and choose **Allow** when it asks "Allow USB debugging?".

The TV app's screen shows these steps too, with each one's state.

data_description.port: The TV's ADB port, 5555 unless you changed it.

error.cannot_connect: Can't reach the TV. Check its address and that network debugging is on.
error.not_authorized: The TV didn't allow the connection. Submit again and accept the prompt on the TV within a minute.
error.adb_off: Network debugging is still off on the TV.
error.not_allowed_in_time: Nobody chose Allow on the TV in time. Submit to ask again.

abort.already_configured: This TV is already set up.
abort.adb_off: Network debugging is off on this TV.
abort.wrong_device: That's a different TV. Add it as a new device instead.
abort.already_in_progress: This TV is already being set up.

data.online_lookups: Look up app icons and artwork online
data.dashboard_controls: Dashboards on the TV can control devices

data_description.online_lookups: Names and icons of the TV's apps from Google Play, and covers and posters for what's playing from iTunes and TVmaze. Off keeps everything on your network.
data_description.dashboard_controls: Dashboards shown on the TV sign in as the TV's own user. Off, it's read-only: they show your home, but can't switch anything. On, they can control devices like any user.

apps.title: Apps and inputs on {name}
apps.description: The same switches as the Apps section of the TV app: change them here or on the TV.

data_description.apps_shown: In the TV's app list (Source) and with a button. An app left out has its button disabled; enabling the button brings it back.
data_description.popups_apps: Notifications pop up while one of these is on screen. Over the others, they go to the notification panel (or nowhere, as the TV app's set).
data_description.inputs_shown: In the TV's source list and its Input picker.
data_description.popups_inputs: The same, for the HDMI inputs.

error.cannot_connect: Couldn't reach the TV app: the change is made when it's back.

abort.not_loaded: The TV isn't set up right now: try again once it is.

command_failed.message: The TV didn't take the command: {error}

unknown_source.message: The TV has no app or input called {source}.

unsupported_media_type.message: Raineworks TV plays audio, video, images, an app, an input or a url, not {media_type}.

unreachable.message: The TV is off its network and Home Assistant doesn't know its network address (MAC) to wake it. Turn on its network standby (Sony: Remote start) so it stays reachable.

bridge_not_paired.message: The TV app (Raineworks TV) isn't installed and paired on this TV. Install it with the Install the TV app action (googletv.install_tv_bridge).

nothing_to_show.message: Give a message, title, image, video or camera to show.

no_owner.message: Finish setting up Home Assistant (its owner's account) before showing a dashboard on the TV.

needs_adb.message: {error}. This TV is connected through its app alone: turn on network debugging on the TV (the TV app's screen shows how), then Reconfigure the TV in Home Assistant and choose Connect over ADB.

bridge_from_play.message: The TV app on this TV is from Google Play, which keeps it up to date. Home Assistant doesn't install over it.

notify.name: Show a notification
notify.description: Shows a notification on the TV through its app (Raineworks TV): a pop-up over whatever's on screen (apps and HDMI inputs), in the notification panel, or both.

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: The badge's icon: a Home Assistant icon (mdi:doorbell), or an image URL or path. The Raineworks TV logo if not set.

image.name: Image
image.description: An image URL, or a Home Assistant path (/local/…, /api/…).

video.name: Video
video.description: A video or live stream URL (HLS, RTSP, MP4), or a Home Assistant path.

camera_entity.name: Camera
camera_entity.description: A camera to show: its live stream, or a snapshot.

camera_view.name: Camera view
camera_view.description: Live: WebRTC when the camera offers it (about a second to start), else HLS. HLS only, or a snapshot. The camera's snapshot shows until the video starts, unless an image is given.

mode.name: Where
mode.description: A pop-up over what's on screen, the notification panel, or both.

position.name: Position
position.description: Where on screen the pop-up goes; the TV's own setting if not set.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long the pop-up stays (8 seconds, 20 with a video, if not set). 0: until it's dismissed, or until the entity below changes.

until_entity.name: Until
until_entity.description: Keep it up until this entity changes (the door closes), then take it down. It stays across restarts of Home Assistant and the TV.

until_state.name: Until state
until_state.description: Take it down when the entity reaches this state, not at any change.

progress.name: Progress
progress.description: A progress bar, 0 to 100: send again with the same tag to move it.

actions.name: Actions
actions.description: Up to 3 buttons, each an action (its id) and a title. The card takes the remote's focus; a button pressed fires googletv_event (type notification_action) with its action and the notification's tag, and Back dismisses it (notification_dismissed). 30 seconds on screen unless the duration says.

size.name: Size
size.description: The pop-up's size; the TV's own setting if not set.

color.name: Color
color.description: The pop-up's border, a hex color.

tag.name: Tag
tag.description: Send again with the same tag to update it in place (a camera keeps playing); dismiss it by its tag.

ignore_rules.name: Ignore rules
ignore_rules.description: Pop up even over apps and inputs the rules exclude.

when_blocked.name: When blocked
when_blocked.description: A pop-up the rules keep off the screen goes to the panel, or nowhere.

dismiss_notifications.name: Dismiss notifications
dismiss_notifications.description: Takes notifications down, from the screen and the notification panel: the one with a tag, else all.

set_notification_rules.name: Set notification rules
set_notification_rules.description: The apps and inputs pop-ups don't show over (by name or id), and what happens to those notifications.

blocked_apps.name: Blocked apps
blocked_apps.description: Apps by name (Netflix) or package (com.netflix.ninja). Replaces the list.

blocked_inputs.name: Blocked inputs
blocked_inputs.description: Inputs by name (Xbox, HDMI 2) or id. Replaces the list.

when_blocked.name: When blocked
when_blocked.description: A blocked pop-up goes to the panel, or nowhere.

show_dashboard.name: Show a dashboard
show_dashboard.description: Shows a Home Assistant dashboard full screen on the TV, through the TV app. It signs in as the TV's own user (made the first time, in Settings → People → Users): read-only unless the TV's options let dashboards control devices. Back, or the media player's stop, closes it.

dashboard.name: Dashboard
dashboard.description: The dashboard's path: lovelace (the Overview), or another's (dashboard-tv).

view.name: View
view.description: A view's path or number; its first view if not set.

install_tv_bridge.name: Install the TV app
install_tv_bridge.description: Installs or updates the TV app (Raineworks TV) over ADB, allows its pop-ups, and pairs with it.

development.name: Development build
development.description: Master's latest build instead of the latest release.

options.live: Live (WebRTC when the camera has it)

confirm.title: Install the TV app on {name}
confirm.description: Home Assistant reaches {name} over ADB, but the TV app (Raineworks TV) isn't on it. The app shows Home Assistant's notifications on the TV, plays its media and dashboards, and tells it what happens there. Submit to install it over ADB now (a minute or so); it's paired by itself.

abort.tv_removed: The TV isn't set up anymore.

update_tv_app.title: Update the TV app on {name}
update_tv_app.description: The TV app on {name} is version {version}; this integration is {latest}. Home Assistant reaches {name} through the app alone, so it can't update it: install the latest app on the TV, or connect over ADB (the TV's ⋮ → Reconfigure) and Home Assistant keeps it up to date by itself.
